findings.title: GitHub Advisory Database: @ethersphere/bee-js 13.3.0 malicious package (GHSA-hh7j-5m3j-23pf)
findings.summary_md: The GitHub Advisory Database flags @ethersphere/bee-js 13.3.0 as embedded malicious code and states that any computer with the package installed or running should be considered fully compromised. All secrets and keys on that machine should be rotated immediately from a different computer, and the package removed, though full control may persist. The advisory was published on 2026-11-09.

findings.title: ethersphere/bee-js npm package version 13.3.0 is compromised (GitHub issue #1294)
findings.summary_md: StepSecurity researcher Ashish Kurmi opened this issue reporting that @ethersphere/bee-js 13.3.0 is compromised and linking to StepSecurity's analysis. It is the earliest public researcher disclosure of the malicious release, created at 00:53:54 UTC on 2026-11-09, before the GitHub advisory and news coverage.

findings.title: Swarm Desktop 0.56.2 is compromised (GitHub issue #581)
findings.summary_md: KunalSin9h reported that Swarm Desktop v0.56.2 is malicious, noting it was published by bee-worker at 2026-11-09 00:36 UTC as an emergency patch release about 30 minutes after the compromised bee-js package. The issue links the malicious commit and SafeDep's analysis. Created at 07:00:25 UTC on 2026-11-09.

findings.title: Malicious @ethersphere/bee-js 13.3.0 Targets Swarm Wallets - Ostorlab
findings.summary_md: Ostorlab's write-up describes the compromised @ethersphere/bee-js 13.3.0 release running a postinstall payload that targets Swarm Desktop wallets and installs remote access, and recommends removing the package and rotating keys. It cites StepSecurity's analysis and the GitHub advisory GHSA-hh7j-5m3j-23pf. Published at 07:30 UTC on 2026-11-09.

findings.title: Ethersphere Hijacked With Crypto Stealing Malware Via Github and npm - OX Security
findings.summary_md: OX Security researchers identified a coordinated supply-chain compromise affecting the Ethersphere ecosystem, in which threat actors leveraged a stolen API key or similar access to commit the same malicious pattern to both the bee-js and swarm-desktop repositories. The post covers the malicious versions bee-js 13.3.0 and Swarm Desktop 0.56.2. Published at 09:29:08 UTC on 2026-11-09.

findings.title: Malicious bee-js npm Release and Swarm Desktop Releases Deliver SleepyDuck Ethereum C2 Backdoor - Socket
findings.summary_md: Socket's Threat Research Team analyzed the November 9, 2026 compromise of Ethersphere's release pipeline, in which a threat actor used the project's own GitHub automation to publish malicious @ethersphere/bee-js 13.3.0 and Swarm Desktop 0.56.2. Socket records that npm received 13.3.0 at 00:09:50 UTC, removed it at 01:24:58 UTC, and that GitHub issued GHSA-hh7j-5m3j-23pf at 01:25:27 UTC. Published at 14:52:15 UTC on 2026-11-09.

findings.title: Hackers Compromise Ethersphere's bee-js and Swarm Desktop to Deliver Wallet-Stealing Malware - The Hacker News
findings.summary_md: The Hacker News reports that attackers abused Ethersphere's release workflows to distribute malicious bee-js 13.3.0 and Swarm Desktop 0.56.2 builds that steal wallet keys and install backdoors. It summarizes the supply-chain compromise and the affected versions for a general security audience. Published at 17:36 UTC on 2026-11-09.
